subject: StellarData discovery — leadership recap, risk map, and procurement path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jim Nolan <jim.nolan@stellardata.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@stellardata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: StellarData discovery — leadership recap & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — wanted to capture the high-level leadership recap so we have a single place for the execs and procurement team to reference. Short summary below and a proposed path to pilot/procurement.

Key business pains (StellarData):
- Inference tail latency spikes during nightly batch scoring and peak query windows (current 90th pctl > 500ms).
- Unpredictable per-token costs across different model sizes; large variance month-to-month for forecasting.
- Data residency & auditability requirements for EU customers and regulated verticals.

Desired outcomes (as discussed):
1) Reduce 90th pctl latency for customer-facing model calls to <150ms and keep p50 < 80ms.
2) Establish predictable monthly unit economics (pilot burn rate cap, followed by reserved capacity).
3) Maintain audit logs and retention policy compatible with SOC2 and upcoming regional compliance.

Risk map / open technical questions:
- SSO + SCIM integration effort for employee access (estimated 1 sprint if SAML ready).
- Logging/retention: need clarification on retention windows and log export format (syslog vs. cloud storage).
- Model packaging: how your infra expects KV cache to be handled across multi-tenant workloads.

Proposed buying path (recommended):
1) 2–4 week pilot (sandboxed tenant in our hosted environment) — prove latency and cost with representative traffic.
2) 3-month pilot reserve (small dedicated pool) to capture steady-state metrics and collect compliance artifacts.
3) Dedicated capacity + enterprise contract (MSA + SOW) for production rollouts across EU/US.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can procurement confirm primary contact and target PO timeline? (I captured procurement@stellardata.com)
- Jim — could you send the 2–3 example queries (payload sizes and concurrency) you mentioned so we can baseline pilot configuration?
- I'll loop in pricing and compliance (Laura, Priya) for a pilot estimate and SOC2/data residency note.

Attachments: [Attachment: stellardata_pilot_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF) — scope & tech checklist]

Proposed timeline: kickoff week of Aug 10 for sandbox pilot; pilot reserve decision by Sep 1 to meet Q4 rollout objectives.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Jim Nolan <jim.nolan@stellardata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@stellardata.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellardata.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarData discovery — leadership recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with our internal read. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Priorities: latency is the gating metric for the product team; cost predictability is the gating metric for the finance/ops team. We can treat them as parallel tracks.
2) Example payloads: attaching the RFP sample and a short payload extract. The calls we care about are synchronous customer lookups (avg payload ~1.6KB, peak concurrency ~120) and nightly batch scoring (avg 20k requests, large sequences).
3) Compliance: SOC2 is non-negotiable for any reserved capacity. We need a short one-page statement that describes where customer data is stored and how audit logs are exported. Can you provide that?
4) Commercial cadence: procurement will look to get a pilot PO in ~3–5 weeks after we have scope/pricing. We can be flexible, but need clear milestones.

Forwarding procurement requests to Claire/Procurement. Laura/Priya — we will need a tight pilot proposal and a clear statement on data handling.

[Attachment: stellardata_rfp.docx (DOCX) — sanitized sample payloads]

—Jim
Jim Nolan
VP, Product — StellarData
jim.nolan@stellardata.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jim Nolan <jim.nolan@stellardata.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@stellardata.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: StellarData discovery — leadership recap & next steps (pricing/compliance asks)

Laura / Priya — looping you in to action Jim's asks. Key items below (quoted from Jim):

- Pilot scope: sandbox + 3-month reserved capacity. Representative traffic: sync calls ~1.6KB payload @ 120 concurrency peak, nightly batch ~20k large seq calls.
- Compliance: 1-page data residency/SOC2 statement and list of artifacts we can produce during the pilot.
- Commercial: pilot PO in 3–5 weeks; provide pricing options (pilot discount vs standard reserved).

Can you please: 
- Laura: quick pilot estimate (cost range for a 3-month small reserved pool + projected token burn with and without caching). Prefer a line-item table we can forward to procurement.
- Priya: draft the 1-page SOC2/data residency note and list of deliverables (audit logs, retention policy, encryption at rest/in transit). Also flag any legal/contract blockers for an EU tenant.

I attached the playbook and a CSV with the proposed pilot scope for quick numbers. Let me know if you need a short call with Jim to walk through payload characteristics.

Attachments: [Attachment: pilot_scope_table.csv (CSV) — pilot traffic & config]

Thanks —
Ben
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@stellardata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jim Nolan <jim.nolan@stellardata.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarData discovery — leadership recap & next steps

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement confirms receipt of the playbook and RFP sample. A couple quick notes from our side:

- Procurement timeline: target to issue a pilot PO within 3–4 weeks after we receive formal scope & pricing. If pricing and SOC2 statement are available by end of next week, we should hit that window.
- Contract ask: we will need a standard MSA + SOW for the pilot with a 30-day termination clause. Any redlines should be flagged early.
- Data residency: we need confirmation we can restrict EU pilot data to EU-hosted instances and receive logs in S3-compatible export.

We'll review the pilot numbers once Laura shares them. For now, Claire on procurement is our point for contracts.

Regards,
Claire Zhou
Head of Ops, StellarData
procurement@stellardata.com
